messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: high error rate from serving-runtime pool 'eu-west-rt' — 5xx spike, autoscaler activity > 120% sustained for 3m. Alert groups: latency, pod_crashloop, OOM_killed

oncall-sre-jake: got the page, i'm on it. pinging @maria-prod for customer impact.

maria-prod: seeing elevated 5xx for a handful of premium customers in EU, some 503s. They're reporting degraded responses. holding customer comms -> @cust-success-emma aware.

ryan-runtime: digging into runtime logs. early signs of CUDA OOMs followed by container crashloop on a subset of replicas. autoscaler kept adding nodes but pods crash on start -> thrash loop.

alex-infra: checking node events — multiple node flaps in the govc cluster; instances showing kernel OOM messages and GPU driver restarts. Could be a bad driver + scale rate combo.

oncall-sre-jake: timeline pls — when did autoscale kick?

alerts-bot: autoscaler: scale_up 2025-11-04T14:12:03Z (+12 nodes) -> scale_down 2025-11-04T14:13:21Z (-10 nodes) -> scale_up 2025-11-04T14:14:05Z (+11 nodes) -> repeated 8x in 6m.

ryan-runtime: looks like model spin-up is failing when sequence length spike + warmed KV cache combined with a quantized kernel path. Example log from crashed pod:
```
2025-11-04T14:14:11Z runtime ERROR CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY: failed to allocate 2.1GB
2025-11-04T14:14:11Z runtime INFO pid=2034 restarting process
2025-11-04T14:14:12Z kubelet WARN BackOff restarting failed container
```

maria-prod: customers seeing 50-80% increased tail latency and intermittent 503. One team reported an internal batch job hitting inference endpoints -> likely traffic spike + autoscaler overreact.

oncall-sre-jake: immediate mitigations: 1) pause autoscaler (scale to stable min), 2) cordon new nodes to prevent more flaky hosts, 3) roll services to smaller model variant fallback. Anyone object?

alex-infra: I'll initiate cluster autoscaler freeze for the EU pool now. running:
```
kubectl annotate deployment autoscaler-control freeze=true -n infra
```
Doing cordon on recently created nodes: `kubectl cordon gpu-eu-*-temp`

sre_lead_olivia: agree with temporary freeze. Also set policy to avoid scale-down for 15m to prevent oscillation.

eng-runtime: can we route traffic to older, stable runtime group in us-west as fallback for critical customers? We have cross-region routing but need to confirm latency/SLA.

maria-prod: do that for the top 3 affected customers. I'll coordinate with @cust-success-emma for messages.

ryan-runtime: launching quick patch: disable quantized kernel path for new pods (env FLAG_DISABLE_QUANT_KERN=true) and increase GPU reserved mem to avoid immediate OOM. Patch applied to canary; monitoring logs.

incident-bot: deploy-bot started rollout: runtime/eu-west -> patch env FLAG_DISABLE_QUANT_KERN=true (canary 1/50).

alerts-bot: within 90s after canary patch, canary pod stable. Error rate on canary host dropped to baseline.

oncall-sre-jake: good sign. start controlled rollout if no regressions. keep autoscaler frozen until roll completes.

alex-infra: Freeze enforced. I set cluster-autoscaler flagged: `--scale-down-disabled` true for 15m.

cust-success-emma: drafting message to affected customers: short note explaining degraded responses, we are routing traffic and applying fixes, ETA 30-45m. Will post after you confirm routing change.

maria-prod: go ahead. include that we may route to us-west for critical flows.

ryan-runtime: rolling patch to remaining replicas now. command: `kubectl set env deployment/runtime FLAG_DISABLE_QUANT_KERN=true -n runtime` -> rolling 10 pods at a time.

eng-runtime: routing update: applying traffic rule for top3 customers -> route to us-west fallback pool with model pin older-1.2. Doing blue/green cutover for those routes.

alerts-bot: 5xx rate started decreasing after 7 minutes, from 12% -> 2.1%. Pod crashloop events decreased by 80%.

oncall-sre-jake: continuing to monitor. next steps: let rollout finish, keep autoscaler frozen, cordon unstable nodes, open postmortem ticket and capture sequence length / batch metrics that triggered quant kernel path. @ryan-runtime and @alex-infra own follow-up.

sre_lead_olivia: escalate to infra patch: please collect dmesg and nvidia-smi logs from flapped nodes. we need to confirm driver/firmware interaction.

alex-infra: grabbing logs now, will attach to incident ticket. quick snippet:
```
[  +0.012345] Out of memory: Kill process 2034 (runtime) score 987 or sacrifice child
NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, pid=2034 Ch 0000001a
```

maria-prod: customer communications sent. two customers responded asking for timeline; cust-success coordinating one-off reroutes for urgent traffic.

oncall-sre-jake: update ETA: stabilization in 20m if no regression. after that we can unfreeze autoscaler with conservative limits.

eng-runtime: monitoring cumulative token throughput; KV cache warmup spikes correlated with batch job at 14:10 which explains sudden mem pressure. We'll recommend rate-limiter rules for large internal jobs.

alerts-bot: incident summary metrics (14:10-14:30): peak 5xx=14%, avg tail latency +420ms, crashloop pods 37 -> 6 after mitigations.

cust-success-emma: customers acknowledged. one asked for root cause once available. Will pass along final postmortem.

ryan-runtime: next steps recorded: 1) revert quant kernel gating until we can repro locally. 2) add guardrail to autoscaler to limit scale-rate to 6 nodes/5m. 3) add prestart memory check for pods to fail-fast and avoid churn. 4) create eval harness to replay KV warmup sequences.

sre_lead_olivia: good. assign follow-ups and open JIRA: INF-5423 (autoscaler rate-limit + cluster freeze playbook), INF-5424 (driver logs + node health), INF-5425 (runtime kernel gating test).

noncall-sre-jake: handing off to overnight on-call @sre_lead_olivia for monitoring and to close once metrics stable for 2h. Please ack.

sre_lead_olivia: acked, taking over. thanks everyone. final note: we'll run a controlled chaos test in staging for autoscaler+driver interactions to avoid recurrence.

incident-bot: INCIDENT: mitigated -> monitoring. Severity downgraded to SEV3. Follow-ups filed: INF-5423, INF-5424, INF-5425.
